name: Electricians
seoTitle: AI Website Audit for Electricians — Free Website Health Check
metaDescription: Free AI website audit built for electricians. Find out why your site isn't winning more callouts, quotes and contracts — in under 30 seconds.
intro: When someone's fuse box has just tripped or they need a rewire quoted, they search on their phone and call whoever looks most trustworthy in the first few results. For electricians, a website's job isn't to look clever — it's to prove you're qualified, local, and easy to reach right now.
painPoints: No visible NICEIC/NAPIT accreditation or Part P certification badges, so visitors can't quickly verify you're qualified to work on their property
Phone number buried below the fold or missing entirely on mobile, losing emergency callout enquiries to a competitor one scroll away
No dedicated pages for the different towns or suburbs covered, so the site never shows up for "electrician near me" searches outside the immediate area
Slow-loading photo galleries of past work that push the call-to-action off-screen on mobile, where most callout searches happen
whyItMatters: Electrical work is a trust-and-urgency purchase — most enquiries happen when something's already gone wrong, so the businesses that convert are the ones that load fast, prove credentials instantly, and make calling or requesting a quote obvious within seconds. A slow, generic-looking site doesn't just lose SEO rankings, it loses the customer to whichever competitor answers the phone first.

faq.question: What should an electrician's website include to win more work?
faq.answer: Visible accreditation (NICEIC/NAPIT/Part P), a phone number that's clickable and visible without scrolling on mobile, genuine customer reviews, clear service areas, and a fast-loading gallery of completed work — all things our free audit checks automatically.

faq.question: Why do I need location pages if I already show up on Google Maps?
faq.answer: Google Business Profile handles local map results, but a dedicated page per town you cover (e.g. "Electrician in Ilford") gives Google separate, indexable content to rank for each area's searches — Maps and website SEO work together, not instead of each other.

faq.question: How fast should an electrician's website load?
faq.answer: Under 2.5 seconds for the main content to appear (Largest Contentful Paint) is the benchmark Google uses — slower than that and you're losing both search ranking and impatient mobile visitors searching mid-emergency.
